headline: Preliminary count at 46.1% of voting places: Labour 29.6%, National 29.4%
body: Updated preliminary party-vote figures carried by RNZ, using Electoral Commission data, put Labour on 29.6% and National on 29.4%, with the Greens on 13.9%, ACT on 10.7%, NZ First on 9.5%, Opportunity on 5.5% and Te Pāti Māori on 0.6%. RNZ’s seat table, supplied by the Commission, shows National on 41 seats, Labour 36, Greens 17, ACT 13, NZ First 11, Opportunity 7 and Te Pāti Māori 5, for a 130-seat Parliament with overhang. These figures cover the 46.1% of voting places that had reported, not 46.1% of votes. Electorate seats in that table are current leads, not confirmed wins. Preliminary results leave out special votes and will change as counting continues. Official results are expected on 27 November.

headline: First preliminary party vote: National ahead with 8.2% of voting places reported
body: Early preliminary figures carried by RNZ, using Electoral Commission data, show National on 31.2% of the party vote and Labour on 28.4%, followed by the Greens (12.8%), ACT (11.2%), NZ First (9.7%) and Opportunity (5.7%). These figures cover only the 8.2% of voting places that had reported, not 8.2% of votes. Preliminary results leave out special votes and will change as counting goes on. Official results are expected on 27 November.
